hook.line: In a story or a report, the order of events matters: one thing happened and then another, or two things collided. Spanish uses two tiny words before an infinitive to tell those apart.

examples.es: Al firmar, se dio cuenta del error.
examples.en: As he signed, he noticed the mistake.
After opening the door, I went in.

examples.es: Al abrir la puerta, vi a Simón.
examples.en: On opening the door, I saw Simón.

examples.es: Tras leer el acta, Mariana llamó a su jefe.
examples.en: After reading the minutes, Mariana called her boss.

examples.es: Al leer el acta, Mariana se rio.
examples.en: As Mariana read the minutes, she laughed.

rule:
Both go before an infinitive, and the person doing it is usually the same person as in the main verb. But they answer different questions.

*Tras* + infinitive: after. The first thing is finished, then comes the next. *Tras firmar, se fue.*

*Al* + infinitive: at that very moment. The two things touch, or the first sets off the second. *Al firmar, se dio cuenta del error.*

Think "after signing" for *tras*, and "on signing" or "as he signed" for *al*. Never use an *-ando* form after either.
smallPrint: Teachers call these prepositional time clauses: *tras* marks what comes before in sequence, and *al* marks coincidence.

options: As he signed, he noticed the mistake.
After signing, he left.
Before signing, he left.

readAndPick.es: Al firmar, se dio cuenta del error.
options: As he signed, he noticed the mistake.
After signing, he fixed the mistake.
He never signed.
As I opened the door, I went in.
I couldn't open the door.
After opening the door, I went in.
After leaving, I called Hernando.
As I left, I saw Hernando.
Hernando saw me leave.

readAndPick.es: Tras la votación, todos se fueron.
options: After the vote, everyone left.
During the vote, everyone left.
Everyone left before the vote.

readAndPick.es: Al oír la noticia, Vale no dijo nada.
options: After telling the news, Vale said nothing.
Vale said nothing about the news.
On hearing the news, Vale said nothing.

readAndPick.es: Tras oír la noticia, Vale llamó a Tomás.
options: After hearing the news, Vale called Tomás.
As she heard the news, Vale was calling Tomás.
Vale called Tomás to give him the news.

readAndPick.es: Al llegar, vi que Vale ya estaba allí.
options: After arriving, Vale left.
On arriving, I saw that Vale was already there.
Vale arrived after me.

readAndPick.es: Tras llegar a casa, llamé a mi mamá.
options: As I got home, I was calling my mum.
My mum called me at home.
After getting home, I called my mum.

yourTurn.prompt: After signing the contract, Tomás felt bad. Choose *Tras* or *Al*: ___ firmar el contrato, Tomás se sintió mal.
yourTurn.answer: Tras firmar el contrato, Tomás se sintió mal.
accept: Tras firmar el contrato, Tomás se sintió mal
yourTurn.why: It says "after", so one thing finishes before the next: *tras*.

yourTurn.prompt: As she read the minutes, Mariana laughed. Choose *Tras* or *Al*: ___ leer el acta, Mariana se rio.
yourTurn.answer: Al leer el acta, Mariana se rio.
accept: Al leer el acta, Mariana se rio
yourTurn.why: The reading sets off the laugh at once, so it is *al*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: After leaving the bank, I had a tinto.
yourTurn.answer: Tras salir del banco, tomé un tinto.
accept: Tras salir del banco, tomé un tinto
Tras salir del banco tomé un tinto.
yourTurn.why: *Tras* + infinitive gives the step before the next one.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: On opening the door, I saw Simón.
yourTurn.answer: Al abrir la puerta, vi a Simón.
accept: Al abrir la puerta, vi a Simón
Al abrir la puerta vi a Simón.
yourTurn.why: *Al* + infinitive: the sighting happens as the door opens.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: After the meeting ended, everyone had a tinto.
yourTurn.answer: Tras terminar la reunión, todos tomaron un tinto.
accept: Tras terminar la reunión, todos tomaron un tinto
Tras terminar la reunión todos tomaron un tinto.
Tras la reunión, todos tomaron un tinto.
yourTurn.why: The meeting is over first, so *tras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Change "after" to "as": Tras entrar, Tomás saludó a todos.
yourTurn.answer: Al entrar, Tomás saludó a todos.
accept: Al entrar, Tomás saludó a todos
Al entrar Tomás saludó a todos.
yourTurn.why: Swap *tras* for *al* and the greeting happens as he comes in.

yourTurn.prompt: Change "as" to "after": Al votar, Hernando miró a Tomás.
yourTurn.answer: Tras votar, Hernando miró a Tomás.
accept: Tras votar, Hernando miró a Tomás
Tras votar Hernando miró a Tomás.
yourTurn.why: Swap *al* for *tras* and the look comes once the voting is done.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Después* needs *de* before an infinitive (*después de firmar*); *tras* doesn't.

pitfalls.wrong: Al firmando, se dio cuenta del error.
pitfalls.right: Al firmar, se dio cuenta del error.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Al* takes a plain infinitive, never an *-ando* form.
Almost. *Al* means "as he signed"; for signing and then leaving, use *tras*.

personal: Think of your morning. Say one thing you do after another, and one thing you notice at a certain moment: *Tras…, …* and *Al…, …*
